title: 2 Pfennigs (magnetic)

obverse.description: An oak seedling with the country name around the rim and the date below.

reverse.description: The mintmark in between two rye ears above the denomination.

comments:
1970J - large / small J

1971J - large / small J

1972J - large / small J

1977F - rye ears (awns)

 

 


Obverse
Numbering of leaves:
1 - top center,
2 - top left,
3 - top right,
4 - bottom left,
5 - bottom right.

Type 1 - bulge script, narrow high connected stalks, leaves 2 and 3 connect to stem by bulges.
Type 2 - bulge script, narrow high connected stalks, leaves 2 and 3 connect to stem by curved lines.
Type 3 - flat script, thick date, "1" with long nose, bold low connected leaves 4 and 5, bulged connection of the leaf 5 with branch.
Type 4 - flat script, thin date, "1" with short nose, bulged connection of the leaf 5 with branch.
Type 5 - flat script, thin date, "1" with short nose, straight low connection of the leaf 5 with branch, leaves 2 and 3 connect by sides to stem.
Type 6 - flat script, thin date, "1" with short wide nose, straight low connection of the leaf 5 with branch, leaf 2 connects to stem higher than leaf 3.
Type 7 - flat script, thin date, "1" with short thin nose, high connection of the leaf 5 with branch produces bulge, straight connection of leaf 2 to stem.
Picture: © Images courtesy of Alexandr Prokofyev.


Reverse
Die A - small grains, lower grains without awns, top end of "G" of PFENNIG to center of vertical stroke, horizontal stroke of "2" with sharper right side.
Die B - large tall grains with awns, top end of "G" of PFENNIG to the right of vertical stroke, the letter wider open, horizontal stroke of "2" with blunter right side.
Picture: © Images courtesy of Alexandr Prokofyev.


There are different styles such as of awn connections with grains, mutual grain position, thickness of details, usually the same for one mint. Following photos demonstrate an example, when all top awns connected with grains on the left photos and most of them ends next to grains on the right photos.
Picture: © Images courtesy of Alexandr Prokofyev.


Combinations
In this section year means production by all mints, being specific mint mentioned separately. For example, "1950" means that coins from all mints D, F, G and J are known, "1958 F" means that coins of only 1958 F are known.

Non-magnetic
1+A: 1950, 1958 F.
2+A: 1958 DGJ, 1959-1968, 1969J.

Magnetic
2+A: 1967 G PS, 1968-1969, 1970 DFG, 1970 small J, 1970 large J.
3+A: 1971.
3+B: 1971, 1971 PS, 1972-1979, 1980 DFJ.
4+B: 1980 G, 1981-1987, 1988 D, 1989.
5+B: 1988, 1990, 1994-1996.
6+B: 1991.
7+B: 1992, 1993.

Abbreviation
PS - proof set.

edge.description: Plain (Copper plating partly stretched over a steel core).
